messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: scale_manual and legend dissappears
parts:
hi everyone,

i want to set a manual scale for shape, but it makes my legend disappear. I haven't found this behaviour so far, am i doing something wrong?

df = data.frame(name = c("a", "b", "c"), var1 = rnorm(3))

ggplot(df, aes(x = name, y = var1)) + geom_point(aes(shape = name)) # with legend

ggplot(df, aes(x = name, y = var1)) + geom_point(aes(shape = name)) + scale_shape_manual(breaks = c(1,2,3), values = c(18,16,21)) #set shapes, legend disappears

I would be glad if someone could give me a hint on that.

Thanks a lot, felix

messages.author: c5246646595bff41
messages.subject: Re: scale_manual and legend dissappears
parts:
Hans,

try:

ggplot(df, aes(x = name, y = var1, shape=name)) + geom_point() + scale_shape_manual(values = c(18,16,21))


HTH

david

messages.subject: Re: scale_manual and legend dissappears
parts:
On Mon, Sep 16, 2013 at 10:27 AM, David Guy
<rstatistica...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hans,
>
> try:
>
> ggplot(df, aes(x = name, y = var1, shape=name)) + geom_point() +
> scale_shape_manual(values = c(18,16,21))

I think this less clear than one might hope, as you are now relying on
the order of the factor levels to map to specific shapes.

The problem with the original example was that the breaks were
specified as c(1, 2, 3), but there were no such values in the name
variable. Correcting this issue in the original example solves the
problem, and makes it clearer that a ==> 18, b ==> 16 and c ==> 21:

scale_shape_manual(breaks = c("a","b","c"), values = c(18,16,21))

Best,
Ista
